rawContent: In 2024, I want a real feminist candidate who made ending sexual violence a core issue from the beginning and lives those beliefs. After the #MeToo movement, how is this really too much to ask for?

This one is also literally not believing other survivors who came forward during #MeToo. Regardless of the actions of some prominent media-appointed #MeToo figureheads, everyone else still deserves your support.

“This is proof that #MeToo was just white feminism. All they wanted was attention.”

#MeToo was founded by a black feminist whose work you are erasing. And the idea that women “cry rape” for attention is a particularly harmful rape myth.

@IramiOF I think those of us who actually do anti-violence work see #MeToo very differently than the general public. #MeToo in the media is different than the movement itself—which is very heavily focused on intersectionality and supporting survivors.

Why is this so important? Because articles like the one in The Nation do real damage to survivors. In the #MeToo era, we have come to see multiple victims as a sign that the allegations against a rapist are real. But it shouldn't be the only way to verify a victim's story.

@WMurphyLaw Not sure I’d say that about #MeToo, but I would definitely say it about the version of #MeToo we get from journalists. And all the backlash that they inspire with their splashy titles and over-simplified versions of accountability. It has been a MESS.

@WMurphyLaw I think there is from Tarana Burke’s #MeToo! It’s just a very different ask than we have been taught to expect of the movement. Very survivor focused, much less concerned with perpetrators than the media on #MeToo.

@WMurphyLaw I agree that the #MeToo movement doesn’t have that focus. But let’s not minimize the impact of the movement or the original organization just because the approach is different. Supporting survivors will make it easier for others affected by SV to take on other agendas.

I’m seeing a lot of this critique of Tara Reade. Here’s my take: before #MeToo, many women didn’t tell ANYONE about their assaults. These were not safe (and certainly not newsworthy) stories in 2008. Reade’s story is coming out now because the world is different now.
